mapping_basis: Paper writes 'plP10' (lowercase L), which I read as a spelling variant of pIP10 (a MANC type in type_list.csv), described as 'descending neurons, which target the wing motor region'. The line's hemidrivers (VT040556-AD; VT040347-DBD) match kit row SS46542, but the kit lists that row as UNMAPPED/DNp79 (previous annotation pIP10).
n_flies_note: Experimental males under light: n = 17 (no threat) and n = 20 (threat), per Ext. Data Fig. 4 source data
notes: Behaviour was scored by eye (BORIS) as courtship and defensive indices; courtship includes foreleg tapping, wing extension/vibration, licking and copulation attempts. No leg-specific or locomotion measure was reported for the activation, so the leg fields are not_assessed. The defensive index (escape, freezing) fell to about zero. I coded the behaviour as 'other' (sustained courtship) with wing_or_flight as secondary.
penetrance: Courtship index near 100% and defensive (escape/freezing) index near 0 under LED, with or without threat (Ext. Data Fig. 4a,b)
quote: optogenetic activation of plP10 resulted in high, sustained courtship levels throughout threat delivery
sensory_condition: courtship chamber (20 mm) with a decapitated virgin female, infrared backlight, continuous blue light, with or without an overhead moving-shadow threat
source_locator: Extended Data Fig. 4a,b; main text section '5-HT inhibits central courtship nodes'
stimulation: 660 nm red light, 50 Hz, 30 s continuous (Supplementary Table 4)
title: Mating proximity blinds threat perception.
